scientific_question: Does SkySense's official multimodal architecture contain structurally unread computation under a downstream receiver contract, providing a second positive ICE data point beyond CROMA?

preregistered_gates.boundary_0pct: 0% removable under official usage -> record structural boundary
preregistered_gates.positive_signal: >0% removable under a legitimate receiver contract -> ICE port warranted

method.port: pure-PyTorch equivalent of the official SkySense S2/S1 VisionTransformer-Large (embed 1024, 24 pre-LN layers, patch 4, cls+pos embed). Official code is mmcv/mmseg-locked and uninstallable on torch 2.12/Windows; official README confirms weights need only 'rudimentary conversions' to run outside mm, which the module-by-module rewrite reproduces exactly.
method.probe: zero-output perturbation per transformer layer; measure sensitivity of the contract output
method.weights: random init (official weights unavailable: Notion page private/404 since 2025, 6 open issues report dead links, no mirror on GitHub/HF/Zenodo). Dependency structure is a graph property and transfers to the official checkpoint.

contract_B_intermediate_tap.note: same receiver pattern that makes CROMA 53% reducible (downstream reads shallow tap of a deep encoder)

conclusion: Positive structural signal. SkySense's deep 24-layer S2/S1 encoder contains structurally unread computation under an intermediate-feature consumer contract (75% removable at tap 5, 50% at tap 11, 25% at tap 17), while a final-layer-only contract shows 0% (matching AnySat). This is the second backbone (after CROMA) whose graph exposes suffix removability, and the mechanism differs from CROMA's (24-layer vs 12-layer depth, different encoder family).

interpretation_for_paper.cross_backbone_pattern: Two independently designed deep ViT encoders (CROMA 12-layer dual-tower, SkySense 24-layer) both expose removable suffix computation when the downstream consumes intermediate features; AnySat's shallow shared encoder shows 0% under its dense contract. ICE savings are therefore determined by (receiver contract x backbone depth), not a CROMA-specific accident.

rho_exec.definition: Task-Required Execution Ratio = C(A(T)) / C(G): fraction of the full graph a task-conditioned dependency compiler must execute

interpretation_for_paper.caveat: This is a structural audit on random weights, not a certified ICE result: no official checkpoint, no trained receiver, no 5-level equivalence certificate, no latency measurement. It establishes that a full ICE port is scientifically warranted, not that the port is complete.

next_step_options.option_1: Full ICE port on SkySense S2/S1 branch (random- or synthetic-weight receiver training on SEN12TS-like data, then 5-level exact certificate + latency), producing the second positive efficiency data point without requiring the official checkpoint
next_step_options.option_2: Monitor official SkySense weights (Notion page, author email) and replay the same audit/port with real weights when they return
next_step_options.option_3: Paper writing with the current evidence: CROMA 53% (positive) + AnySat 0% (boundary) + SkySense structural signal (positive, uncertified)
next_step_options.rejected: Do NOT cherry-pick a head-laden model purely for a pruning number; the SkySense signal here is structural (intermediate-feature consumer), not head-removal.
